segments.arabic:
١١٢٠٣- ريحانة بنت شمعون
بن زيد «١»، وقيل زيد بن عمرو بن قنافة، بالقاف، أو خنافة بالخاء المعجمة، من بني النضير. وقال ابن إسحاق: من بني عمر بن قريظة: وقال ابن سعد: ريحانة بنت زيد بن عمرو بن خنافة بن شمعون بن زيد من بني النضير، وكانت متزوجة رجلا من بني قريظة يقال له الحكم، ثم روى ذلك عن الواقدي.
قال ابن إسحاق في «الكبرى»: كان رسول اللَّه ﷺ سباها فأبت إلا اليهودية، فوجد رسول اللَّه ﷺ في نفسه، فبينما هو مع أصحابه إذ سمع وقع نعلين خلفه، فقال: هذا ثعلبة بن سعية يبشرني بإسلام ريحانة، فبشره وعرض عليها أن يعتقها ويتزوجها ويضرب عليها الحجاب، فقالت: يا رسول اللَّه، بل تتركني في ملكك، فهو أخف عليّ وعليك، فتركها.
وماتت قبل وفاة رسول اللَّه ﷺ بستة عشر. وقيل لما رجع من حجة الوداع.
وأخرج ابن سعد عن الواقديّ بسند له عن عمر بن الحكم، قال: كانت ريحانة عند زوج لها يحبها، وكانت ذات جمال، فلما سبيت بنو قريظة عرض السبي على النبي ﷺ، فعزلها، ثم أرسلها إلى بيت أم المنذر بنت قيس حتى قتل الأسرى، فرق السبي، فدخل إليها فاختبأت منه حياء. قالت: فدعاني فأجلسني بين يديه وخيرني فاخترت اللَّه ورسوله، فأعتقني وتزوّج بي. فلم تزل عنده حتى ماتت. وكان يستكثر منها ويعطيها ما تسأله، وماتت مرجعه من الحج، ودفنها بالبقيع.
وقال ابن سعد: أخبرنا محمّد بن عمر: قال: حدثني صالح بن جعفر، عن محمد بن كعب، قال: كانت ريحانة مما أفاء اللَّه على رسوله، وكانت جميلة وسيمة، فلما قتل زوجها وقعت في السبي، فخيرها رسول اللَّه ﷺ، فاختارت الإسلام، فأعتقها وتزوجها وضرب عليها الحجاب، فغارت عليه غيرة شديدة فطلقها، فشق عليها وأكثرت البكاء، فراجعها، فكانت عنده حتى ماتت قبل وفاته.
وأخرج من طريق الزّهريّ أنّه لما طلقها كانت في أهلها، فقالت: لا يراني أحد بعده.
قال الواقدي: وهذا وهم، فإنّها توفيت عنده.
(١) أسد الغابة: ت ٦٩٤٢، الاستيعاب: ت ٣٣٩٦.
segments.english:
11203 — Rayhana bint Shamun ibn Zayd¹

Her genealogy is also given as Rayhana bint Zayd ibn Amr ibn Qinafa—with a qaf—or Khinafa, with a dotted kha, of Banu al-Nadir. Ibn Ishaq said that she was from Banu Umar ibn Qurayza. Ibn Sa'd said: Rayhana bint Zayd ibn Amr ibn Khinafa ibn Shamun ibn Zayd, of Banu al-Nadir. She had been married to a man of Banu Qurayza called al-Hakam. He then narrated this from al-Waqidi.

Ibn Ishaq said in al-Kubra: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had taken her captive, but she refused to embrace anything other than Judaism. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, felt distressed. While he was with his Companions, he heard the sound of two sandals behind him and said, “This is Tha'laba ibn Sa'ya bringing me the good news of Rayhana's acceptance of Islam.” Tha'laba gave him the good news. The Prophet offered to emancipate and marry her and to impose the veil upon her. She said, “O Messenger of Allah, instead, leave me in your possession, for that is easier for me and for you.” So he left her as she was.

She died sixteen [months] before the death of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. It is also said that she died when he returned from the Farewell Pilgrimage.

Ibn Sa'd transmitted from al-Waqidi, through a chain of his, from Umar ibn al-Hakam, who said: Rayhana had a husband who loved her, and she was beautiful. When Banu Qurayza were taken captive, the captives were presented to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he set her apart. He then sent her to the house of Umm al-Mundhir bint Qays until the prisoners had been killed and the captives distributed. He entered upon her, but she hid from him out of modesty. She said: “He summoned me, seated me before him, and gave me a choice. I chose Allah and His Messenger, so he emancipated me and married me.” She remained with him until she died. He sought much from her and gave her whatever she asked of him. She died on his return from the pilgrimage, and he buried her in al-Baqi.

Ibn Sa'd said: Muhammad ibn Umar informed us; he said: Salih ibn Ja'far related to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Rayhana was among the fay' that Allah bestowed upon His Messenger. She was beautiful and comely. When her husband was killed, she became one of the captives. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, gave her a choice, and she chose Islam. He therefore emancipated and married her and imposed the veil upon her. She became intensely jealous over him, so he divorced her. This distressed her, and she wept profusely. He then took her back, and she remained with him until she died before his death.

He also transmitted, through al-Zuhri, that when he divorced her, she was among her family and said, “No one shall see me after him.”

Al-Waqidi said: This is an error, for she died while she was with him.

¹ Usd al-Ghaba: entry 6942; al-Isti'ab: entry 3396.

segments.arabic:
وذكر محمّد بن الحسن في أخبار المدينة، عن الدراوَرْديّ، عن سليمان بن بلال، عن يحيى بن سعيد أن رسول اللَّه ﷺ صلّى في منزل من دار قيس بن قهد، وكانت ريحانة القرظية زوج النبي ﷺ تسكنه.
وقال أبو موسى: ذكرها ابن مندة في ترجمة مارية، ولم يفردها بترجمة. وقيل:
اسمها ربيحة- بالتصغير.
قلت: بل أفردها، فإنه قال ما هذا نصه بعد ذكره الأزواج الحرائر: وسبي جويرية في غزوة المريسيع، وهي ابنة الحارث بن أبي ضرار، وسبي صفية بنت حيي بن أخطب من بني النضير، وكانت مما أفاء اللَّه عليه، فقسم لهما، واستسرى جاريته القبطية، فولدت له إبراهيم، واستسرى ريحانة من بني قريظة، ثم أعتقها فلحقت بأهلها، واحتجبت وهي عند أهلها. وهذه فائدة جليلة أغفلها ابن الأثير.
وأخرج ابن سعد عن الواقديّ من عدة طرق- أنه ﷺ تزوّجها وضرب عليها الحجاب، ثم قال: وهذا الأثر عند أهل العلم. وسمعت من يروي أنه كان يطؤها بملك اليمين. وأورد ابن سعد من طريق أيوب بن بشر المعافري- أنها خيرت، فقالت: يا رسول اللَّه، أكون في ملكك فهو أخفّ عليّ وعليك، فكانت في ملكه يطؤها إلى أن ماتت.
segments.english:
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan mentioned in Akhbar al-Madina, from al-Darawardi, from Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, that the Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—prayed in a dwelling in the house of Qays ibn Qahd, in which Rayhana al-Quraziyya, the wife of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—used to reside.

Abu Musa said: Ibn Manda mentioned her in the entry on Mariya and did not give her a separate entry. It is said that her name was Rubayha—in the diminutive form.

I say: Rather, he did give her a separate entry, for after mentioning the free wives he said, in these exact words: “Juwayriyya was taken captive during the expedition of al-Muraysi'; she was the daughter of al-Harith ibn Abi Dirar. Safiyya bint Huyayy ibn Akhtab, of Banu al-Nadir, was taken captive, and she was among that which Allah bestowed upon him as spoils; he allotted [marital turns] to both of them. He took his Coptic slave woman as a concubine, and she bore him Ibrahim. He also took Rayhana of Banu Qurayza as a concubine, then emancipated her, whereupon she rejoined her people and observed the veil while among them.” This is a valuable point that Ibn al-Athir overlooked.

Ibn Sa'd transmitted from al-Waqidi through several routes that he—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—married her and imposed the veil upon her. He then said: “This report is known among the scholars. I have also heard someone relate that he had intercourse with her by virtue of ownership.” Ibn Sa'd also cited, through Ayyub ibn Bishr al-Ma'afiri, that she was offered a choice and said: “O Messenger of Allah, I will remain in your ownership, for that is easier for both you and me.” She therefore remained in his ownership, and he had intercourse with her until she died.
